newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to continue squeezing rupiah liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to continue squeezing rupiah liquidity.

text.p: Indonesia's monetary authority will continue tightening rupiah liquidity in a bid to thwart speculators who have been pressuring the currency's exchange rate against the U.S. dollar, the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Tuesday.

Minister of Economics, Finance and Supervisor of Development, Saleh Afiff, was quoted as saying the tightening would trigger the selling of dollars in favour of the rupiah, allowing the local currency to strengthen.
Afiff said the liquidity tightening was now the "homework" of the finance minister and central bank governor.

"I cannot explain how the further tightening will be carried out. Because it will be done tomorrow (Tuesday)," he told reporters on Monday after a meeting of the monetary authority at the finance ministry which discussed the weakening rupiah.

The meeting was also attended by Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad, central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono, State Secretary Murdiono and economic advisers to the government, Widjojo Nitisastro and Ali Wardana.
The newspaper quoted an analyst as saying the steps could include raising the interest rates of central bank certificates, and a continued freeze on transactions in short-term securities.
